---
title: "Lab 00 — Welcome to R"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("../R/lab_submission.R")
world <- read_csv("data/country_indicators.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab00", title = "Welcome to R")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "What does one row of this dataset represent?",
  q2 = "How many countries are in the file?",
  q3 = "For GDP per capita, which statement is true?",
  q4 = "In one or two sentences, describe the life-expectancy distribution without using a causal verb."
)
```

## What you will do

Load the teaching country file, name the unit of analysis, and read a simple summary. At the end, download a `.txt` with your name, the date, and your answers, and upload that file.

```{r peek, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=4}
glimpse(world)
nrow(world)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("One country", correct = TRUE),
  answer("One year of world population"),
  answer("One variable"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("50", correct = TRUE),
  answer("22"),
  answer("500"),
  allow_retry = TRUE
)
```

```{r gdp-summary, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=5}
world |>
  summarise(
    mean_gdp = mean(gdp_per_capita),
    median_gdp = median(gdp_per_capita)
  )
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("The mean is well above the median: the distribution is right-skewed.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The mean and the median are the same, so GDP is symmetric."),
  answer("The median is larger, so most countries are very rich."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Shape, center, and whether mean or median is more informative.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = shiny::reactiveValuesToList(learnr::get_tutorial_state()),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
